A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRB research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including the additional appendix material in v2.

before.justification: Sections 6 and Appendices E–H report original clustering experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and reports additional sensitivity, diagnostic and ablation results in Appendices E.3 and H.11–H.14.

M1.justification: BRB retains the same soft weight resets, reclustering and centroid momentum resets. Equations (1)–(2), Algorithm 1 and the training objectives are unchanged. Newly specified initialization details and experimental ablation variants do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, KMNIST, FMNIST, USPS, OPTDIGITS, GTSRB, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100-20. Reconstruction-based training with and without pretraining, and contrastive learning with self-labeling, remain the principal scenarios. The added analyses reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The main comparator set, including DEC, IDEC, DCN, SCAN, GCC and SeCu, is retained. New supplementary comparisons introduce perturbation-only and scaled Gaussian weight-noise variants in Figure 19, and BRB using native DEC/IDEC assignments in Tables 18–19.

E3.justification: The added studies introduce controls comparing predicted versus ground-truth labels for silhouette scores, contraction-free versus full resets, and native versus k-Means reassignment with and without pretraining. Existing benchmark preprocessing, architectures, training budgets and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the existing analyses: sensitivity sweeps on USPS and OPTDIGITS (E.3), silhouette scores under different label sources (H.11), reconstruction-error trajectories (H.12), soft-reset component ablations (H.13), and native-assignment versus k-Means reclustering (H.14). These address additional robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 changes the default reporting description from averages over ten seeds with standard deviations to averages over ten runs with standard errors. Explicit standard-deviation captions, including Tables 11, 16 and 17, and existing numerical uncertainty entries remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish increased run counts or recomputed uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, but Figures 9 and 17–19 and Tables 18–19 substantially expand the reported sensitivity, diagnostic and ablation outcomes. For example, Table 19 adds 85.72 accuracy for BRB with native DEC reassignment on pretrained OPTDIGITS, versus the retained k-Means result of 92.32. Table 18 reverses the USPS/OPTDIGITS DEC entries relative to Table 13, leaving those dataset assignments inconsistent.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, distance definitions and runtime-complexity analysis are retained. Equation (19) repeats the existing reset equation rather than introducing new mathematics. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: identifying the reclustering barrier, overcoming it with BRB, enabling training from scratch and achieving competitive contrastive-clustering performance. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New interpretations qualify hyperparameter robustness as dataset-dependent, warn that silhouette scores using predicted labels can mislead, and explain contraction through gradient balancing and reconstruction error as a tradeoff. The new claim of consistently better k-Means reassignment overlooks the pretrained DEC/GTSRB exception in Table 19: 61.73 versus 62.98 for native reassignment.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly specifies Kaiming uniform initialization. Appendix H.13 explains how the Gaussian-noise ablation uses current weight means and standard deviations. Hardware descriptions, principal hyperparameter tables and the code/model access link already appeared in v1; the new reproducibility statement mainly consolidates existing information.

R1.justification: v2 adds He et al. (2015) for initialization and surveys by Lu et al. (2024) and Huang et al. (2024). Positioning relative to deep clustering and reset methods remains substantially unchanged. Publication-year and venue changes for existing works, including Asano and Zhou, do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify reclustering and experimental setup, while Section 6.4 becomes a broader ablation summary. v2 adds appendix subsections and reproducibility and ethics statements, and updates affiliations, headers and bibliography formatting. The original narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with sensitivity matrices in Figure 9, diagnostic and ablation plots in Figures 17–19, and assignment-comparison Tables 18–19. Existing figures and tables are largely retained, with reflow, renumbering and limited caption changes.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity studies extend support beyond MNIST, and the component ablations better substantiate BRB's design choices. Metric and reconstruction diagnostics also improve interpretability. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix E.3 states a learning rate of 0.05 while Figure 9 labels 0.005, and Table 18 conflicts with Table 13's DEC dataset assignments. Overall, v2 provides useful additional support without substantially changing the paper's established findings.
